name: Quantum information: fixed-depth QAOA parameter design
description: Design graph-dependent two-layer QAOA angles maximizing the mean ratio of the independently simulated expected cut to the exact classical optimum on six small graphs. The circuit architecture is fixed; the candidate controls its parameter-selection algorithm.

sources.locator: Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann (2014), Sections I-II, Eqs. (2)-(7), (11)-(12): phase separator, mixer, expected cost and MaxCut Hamiltonian.

requirements.datasets: None downloaded; mathematical constructions or locally generated synthetic instances.

evaluation.benchmark: Quantum information: fixed-depth QAOA parameter design
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: angles(n, edges, p) -> real array (p, 2), rows (gamma, beta) in radians. The fixed circuit starts in |+>^n and applies exp(-i gamma C), then exp(-i beta sum X), for each row; C is unweighted MaxCut. Return angles only. Six public evaluation graphs use n=6,8,10 and densities 0.25,0.55 (seed 713); use graph_cases(seed=113) for separate development graphs. Objective: mean expected-cut/exhaustive-optimum ratio. p=2; no shot noise or timing term.

limitations: Independent ideal statevector reimplementation, not quantum hardware or a reproduction of the paper tables.
Evaluation sizes, graph generator and two-layer budget are local choices. Small graphs can be solved classically; an improved score does not establish quantum advantage.
Public deterministic validation graphs are separate from development seed 113, not hidden. Assess generalization only on fresh graphs after freezing the candidate.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Optimize a two-layer QAOA circuit on six small MaxCut graph instances.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Qualifying evidence that this local task addresses a primary scientific problem has not been established.
science_relevance.reason: The reviewed Farhi et al. paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4028) introduces a general quantum optimization algorithm and analyses MaxCut examples. It does not establish the local six-graph, fixed-depth parameter benchmark as a substantive primary scientific target under the stricter rule. A direct problem-focused justification remains to be established; this is not a claim that MaxCut or quantum optimization lacks scientific value.
